   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

Dear Ron and Brian,

My first attempt to use"TABLOID"
[print option in the Spectrum
version of OUTLET] produced the
enclosed double-spaced print-out
which I could not believe was
what was intended. "Alter your
"DIP" switches" I hear you say
but this is by no means easy on
the LX 80 requiring a dentist's
mirror in one hand, a torch in
the other and a very slim screw-
driver in the...... See what I
mean? - and of course one must
remember to reset afterwards.

To justify my recently acquired
Multiface (more later) and the
resident Genie Disassembler, I
decided to do some hacking and,
using the "Find" function of
Genie,soon identified Line-feeds
followed by Carriage Returns at
31256 and 31478. Poking "0" to
three locations at each address
seemed to do the trick so I
decided to experiment with"Line-
saver" from Issue 035.I inserted
the Pokes after the Go-Sub [Line
1605] and saved it feeling that
to Merge the modified line would
be easier and perhaps more
accurate than individual pokes
of 0 (six times) when each issue
is loaded - somehow I don't like
the idea of re-saving your
exquisite routine - it seems too
much like sacrilege.

Anyway it didn't work as I still
got double spacing - I have no
idea why it worked following
direct pokes but didn't when I
altered line 1605.

Back to the hacking table and,
after a bit of poking around I
realised that the Go-Sub in Line
1605 did not produce the code I
had been looking at, but placed
code around 65000 (exact extent
not identified yet). The Multi-
face then found more Line feeds
at 64971 and 65193. Re-setting
these had the right effect but I
still had extra L/Fs at the end
of each 22 lines (Screen Page?).
These were down to the "L/PRINT
CHR$ VAL "IO" towards the end of
Line 1610 which took quite a bit
of time to edit out.

Back to Linesave and "IT WORKS"!
-but there must be a better way?

1) Could Tabloid have a L/F
option like Tasword and most
other printer drivers?

2) If not, is there a better way
than mine or DipSwitch fiddling?

3) Could we have some help in
understanding your so efficient
Go-Sub 99?? routines which are
carefully hidden behind a screen
of control codes?

4) Have you published a routine
to create these basic lines from
our own code or is it a "Trade
Secret"?

5)Is there a stand-alone version
of TABLOID to use for printing
from earlier issues of OUTLET or
is it necessary (and possible)
to load a file from an earlier
issue into a "Tabloid equipped"
later version? - not tried yet.

6) Is there a routine to LPRINT
the information in articles like
Multistore in Issue 032? There
is an LPRINT option for Multi-
Extra but not for Multistore
which contains much detailed
information.This is inaccessible
if the program is not in memory
and, whilst it can be stored in
Multiface, not when anything
else is there. Multiple Screen
dumps seem clumsy; hand-written
notes from the screen positively
primitive.    - Cliff Jackson

>Cliff Jackson from Brian Cavers

I've made a note to review the
TABLOID BASIC again. The main
problem is there are only a few
hundred bytes free in CONTENTS
as room must be left for various
changeable items (text loads in
at 34568 - only just above the
variables area!).

Most OUTLET machine code is put
in BASIC REM statements around
lines 9900 upward usually. This
saves storage space on disc etc.
(sector use is more efficient),
is far easier reSAVEing programs
(you don't have to worry about
SAVEing CODE - just ONE program)
and LOADing time is faster. CODE
is easily put in REMs using our
REMSTORE (OUTLET 6).

Some of these REMs just move the
code up into memory following
which you use a USR in the usual
way, some jump automatically to
the code and some just run the
code within the REM. These REMs
may look secretive but that is
not by intent - they merely look
meaningless when displayed in a
BASIC LISTing.

As I only have an early version
of Multiface I couldn't test
MULTISTORE so I daren't make any
changes for fear of introducing
a bug I would never know about
(until letters started pouring
in!). In addition, I think there
was not a lot of room for any
addition.Try LLIST 70 to get the
info you want.  - Brian Cavers

RON'S REPLY TO GEORGE BROWN:-
With regard to the Clive Drive.
There is no connection here to
Clive Sinclair - this is just a
legal way of cashing in on the
popularity of a great inventor.
We have no direct experience of
this hardware and therefore have
no grounds to criticise it or

recommend it. However, I would
be concerned to know what type
of disk is being used, how much
they cost to buy and how widely
they were available.I understand
they use a miniature 3" disk
(which is not the same as the
standard 3" disk used by Amstrad
systems) and that they store 50k
on each side. I suspect, if you
use many disks, you could end up
paying more than you think for
this equipment.For instance,with
a standard 3.5" disk used on the
Plus D system it should cost no
more than around 10p per 100K of
data stored - compare this with
microdrive cartridges which cost
around `2.00 per 100K of data
stored! You can see the tremend-
ous difference the cost of the
media makes to a system.

To be honest,I don't think there
is a better buy around at the
moment than the Plus D and drive
from Datel Electronics (around
`130). You would still need a
printer but, if you shop around,
you could purchase a reasonably-
priced thermal printer (say the
HR5) to replace your Timex. Your
initial outlay would be more
than the `149.95 for the Clive
Drive and printer but,I believe,
you could save any diffence in
the first 12 months - there is a
`21 difference between a twelve-
month subscription of OUTLET on
disk and on cartridge, for
example!
                        - Ron

From Malcolm Perry

In all the various comments and
reviews regarding the excellent
+D interface I do not recall
seeing it mentioned that the +D
can be used as a Centronics
printer interface as it stands
without the need to be booted
with a DOS or even having a disc
connected (I did not know this
when I wrote my review as I used
a Disciple which needs to be
Booted to run a printer). This
means that if considering a
Centronics interface but not
being able to afford a full disc
system at the time, the +D will
fulfill this function and has
the advantage it can have discs
added later, as and when funds
become available.

In this unbooted form there are
some restrictions on printer
functions available and it is
set for FX80 compatability. Both
+D and Disciple can be BOOTed
from tape evey time to run a
printer if no drive is available
but it is a slow process and not
(by me) recomended, although it
does give full printer functions
and allow for different printer
types.


This is based on the MGT +D; I
presume the Datel one now being
sold is the same but advise to
check.

The resulting print-out from the
tape cassette LABELMAKER (OUTLET
37)is,as you mention, too narrow
on my LC10 printer driven by
Disciple. With this combination
of system, some very simple
modifications will give better
results. Obviously other systems
may or may not be possible to
alter.The idea is,instead of the
print routine in the program,
COPY SCREENS is used instead and
the printer graphic mode changed
(in the Disciple) to suit which
type of printout is being done.
PLOTTER GRAPHICS (27, 42, 5) is
correct for the cassette label.
This is 72 dots per inch. NORMAL
DENSITY ( 27,42,0 ) is slightly
wider than the insert so needs a
bit of trimming. This is 60 DPI
graphic mode.

Program mods:

Add line 475 LET MODE = 1

Add Line 1525 LET MODE = 2

Alter line 9764 to read(in full)
IF K$ ="D" THEN GO SUB VAL"9784"
: POKE@42,27 : POKE@ 43,42 :
POKE@ 44,5 : IF MODE = 2 THEN
POKE@ 44,0

Add line 9765 IF K$="D" THEN
GOTO 9700.

The next line is left intact for
possible future use and the new
bit is simply added in at the
start.

9769 COPY SCREEN$ : RETURN :
rest of original line follows.

That's it! Save the new version
and it's ready to go (Disciple
users save by GOTO 9982). So now
your labels should not look as
if they've shrunk in the wash!

You will notice the insert print
out is not quite right but just
trim and fold and all is ok and
the discrepancy is not really
noticeable. The problem could be
overcome by either altering the
PLOT and DRAW values or using
the reverse feed of the printer.

         - Malcolm Perry

Thanks, Malcolm.
                 - Brian

Mr. M.E.Tomlin from Brian Cavers

Remember, it's line 1002 in the
LOADER BASIC (filename DISK on a
+3) - not the CONTENTS BASIC. If
you reset the +3 to get the
loader menu then press ENTER to
boot and then hold down BREAK
until the loader has loaded. Now
enter +3 BASIC and you will see
the line.

However, Your letter makes me
wonder if it doesn't work! Have
you tried a print-out?Can anyone
else confirm it's o.k. (I can't
test it myself as I have no
problem with printing on my +3).

Now, regarding extracting code
from our REMs...

Utility programs where the code
is in a REM usually give the
code address and length for any
of you who prefer it so I assume
you mean incidental code in any
OUTLET programs that's in a REM.

Most of our REMs have a name tag
and sometimes I put the start
address, e.g. UDGS TO 65368 or
CHR$ TO 4E4 (40000). If not then
it may not be easy. Reset the
computer so memory is full of
zeros, load the program direct
and then study the BASIC to see
what USR calls there are to give
you some idea of the area the
code is in memory. Try a FOR
NEXT loop PEEKing back and forth
through memory to spot the code.
However, some code is NOT moved

into memory at all! It runs IN
the REM. To extract it you could
put a line in front and use the
NXTLIN system variable at 23637
and PEEK forward from that. Such
code could then be loaded and
run at ANY address.

If you need help with any one in
particular let me know. If you
simply want to use the routines
in your own programs it's far
easier to just delete the other
lines, SAVE the REM line and
MERGE it in your own program. We
have had one or two block delete
programs in OUTLET but I'm not
sure if there has been one since
the +3 version started at Issue
23. Perhaps this is a good case
for re-issuing DELINER (OUTLET
5)?                    - Brian

POKE 23611, PEEK 23611 BAND 223
on SAM before an INPUT stops the
last key pressed character from
appearing in the INPUT (which it
sometimes does).

POKE 23611, 205 on the Spectrum
to get ALL the UDGS available in

I now have a JVC (TM-150 PSN-K)
monitor linked to my SAM via the


SCART socket. It has completely
transformed the quality of the
picture - even 85 columns text
is clear and I can pick out each
colour in the tiny FLASH palette

There was a neat decimal values
print routine(to get the decimal
points all lined up) in John
Wase's "SHORT SPOT" section of
FORMAT magazine the other month.
I devised the following...

  PRINT TAB 10-LEN STR$ INT X;X

         ...where X is the value
to be printed. This works fine
on SAM but needs adjusting to...

 TAB 10-LEN STR$ INT X+(X<.1);X

       ...on the Spectrum (which
PRINTs a zero before values .1
to .9).

From:G.T.Parkyn, TRURO.


Dear Ron Cavers,

Your records will show you that
I have a 48k Spectrum, using a
RAMPRINT interface to drive a
CITIZEN LSP -10 printer. I have
recently acquired a KEMPSTON E
printer interface which I intend
to use with my 128k Spectrum in
48k mode and the same printer.

However,I find that I can obtain
LINE FEED when I have TOKENS ON.
If I set TOKENS OFF there is no
line feed. This, of course means
that I have either the ability
to send printer controls or have
line feed but not both!

I could, of course, set the
internal switches of the printer
to give line feed, but do not
want to do this as my RAMPRINT
interface is set to give LINE
FEED ON, and many of my programs
are written to be compatible
with this.

As a matter of interest,the var-
ious OUTLET printer options work
satisfactorily with your setting
for the KEMPSTON E interface,
with my printer set to give no
line feed.

Can you give me some advice as
to how to obtain LINE FEED ON,
together with TOKENS OFF on the
KEMPSTON E printer interface? Am
I not doing something I should?
                  - G.T. Parkyn

To:G.T. Parkyn from Brian Cavers

The linefeeds MUST be provided
from somewhere and there are 3
possibilities: 1.The printer may
provide them (in your case de-
activated by the dipswitch);  2.
The printer interface may send
them (in your case de-activated
because you have selected TOKENS
OFF on your Kempston E which is
designed NOT to send linefeeds
in that mode); 3. The program or
software sends them.Our software
sends them in text mode which is
why it works o.k. on your setup.

You have little choice but to
set up your programs to send the
linefeed if you need to use the
TOKENS OFF mode.
                   - Brian

PLOTTER GRAPHICS (27, 42, 5) is correct for the cassette label. This is 72 dots per inch. NORMAL DENSITY ( 27,42,0 ) is slightly wider than the insert so needs a bit of trimming. Program mods:

Add line 475 LET MODE = 1

Add Line 1525 LET MODE = 2

Alter line 9764 to read(in full) IF K$ ="D" THEN GO SUB VAL"9784" : POKE@42,27 : POKE@ 43,42 : POKE@ 44,5 : IF MODE = 2 THEN POKE@ 44,0

Add line 9765 IF K$="D" THEN GOTO 9700.

The next line is left intact for possible future use and the new bit is simply added in at the start.

9769 COPY SCREEN$ : RETURN : rest of original line follows.

That's it! Save the new version and it's ready to go (Disciple users save by GOTO 9982). So now your labels should not look as if they've shrunk in the wash!

Распечатка из программы кассетных вкладышей LABELMAKER (OUTLET 37), как вы уже отмечали, получается слишком узкой на моем принтере LC10, подключенном через Disciple. Для этой связки есть очень простая доработка, дающая гораздо лучший результат. Разумеется, на других системах переделка может отличаться или быть вовсе невозможной. Идея в том, чтобы вместо встроенной в программу процедуры печати использовать команду `COPY SCREEN$`, переключая графический режим принтера (в Disciple) в зависимости от того, какая часть распечатывается. Для самой наклейки на кассету подходит режим PLOTTER GRAPHICS (27, 42, 5) — это 72 точки на дюйм. Режим NORMAL DENSITY (27, 42, 0) делает распечатку чуть шире вкладыша, так что придется немного подрезать — это режим 60 DPI.

**Доработки в программе:**

Добавьте строку:
```text
475 LET MODE = 1
```

Добавьте строку:
```text
1525 LET MODE = 2
```

Измените строку 9764 (целиком):
```text
9764 IF K$ ="D" THEN GO SUB VAL"9784" : POKE@ 42,27 : POKE@ 43,42 : POKE@ 44,5 : IF MODE = 2 THEN POKE@ 44,0
```

Добавьте строку:
```text
9765 IF K$="D" THEN GOTO 9700
```

Следующая строка сохраняется для возможного использования в будущем, а новый фрагмент просто дописывается в ее начало:

```text
9769 COPY SCREEN$ : RETURN : ...далее остаток оригинальной строки.
```

### Ответ M.E. Tomlin от Brian Cavers

Помните: строка 1002 находится в LOADER BASIC (файл с именем DISK на +3), а не в CONTENTS BASIC. Если вы перезагрузите +3, чтобы выйти в загрузочное меню, нажмёте ENTER для старта, а затем удержите BREAK, пока лоадер загружается, вы сможете войти в +3 BASIC и увидеть эту строку.

Впрочем, ваше письмо заставило меня усомниться — а работает ли она вообще? Вы пробовали распечатать? Может ли кто-нибудь ещё подтвердить работоспособность? (Сам я протестировать не могу, так как на моём +3 с печатью проблем нет).

Теперь по поводу извлечения кода из наших REM...

В утилитах, где код спрятан в REM, адрес и длина обычно указываются для тех, кому это нужно. Поэтому я полагаю, вы имеете в виду дополнительный код в программах OUTLET, хранящийся в REM.

У большинства наших REM есть метка с именем, а иногда я указываю и начальный адрес, например `UDGS TO 65368` или `CHR$ TO 4E4 (40000)`. Если этого нет, извлечь код может быть непросто. Перезагрузите компьютер, чтобы память очистилась в нули, загрузите программу напрямую и изучите BASIC на предмет вызовов USR, чтобы понять, в какой области памяти он работает. Попробуйте цикл FOR...NEXT с PEEK вперед и назад по памяти, чтобы найти этот код.

Однако некоторый код ВООБЩЕ НЕ перемещается в память! Он выполняется прямо ВНУТРИ строки REM. Чтобы извлечь его, можно вставить перед ним строку, использовать системную переменную NXTLIN по адресу 23637 и считывать PEEK дальше от неё. Такой код потом можно будет загружать и запускать по ЛЮБОМУ адресу.
